summary: When Hezekiah became very sick, he turned his face to the wall, prayed, and cried. God said, 'I have heard your prayer and seen your tears,' healed him, and added fifteen years to his life. The shadow on the stairs went backward as a sign.

story_reel.narration: Some time later, King Hezekiah became so sick that he was close to dying. The prophet Isaiah came to see him and said, 'This is what Yahweh says: Get your house in order, because you won't recover.' Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed, 'Please, Yahweh, remember how I have walked before You faithfully with my whole heart, and have done what is good in Your eyes.' And Hezekiah cried hard. Isaiah hadn't even left the palace courtyard when God spoke to him again. 'Go back and tell Hezekiah: This is what Yahweh, the God of your father David, says: I have heard your prayer. I have seen your tears. I will heal you. I will add fifteen years to your life.' God told Isaiah to put a paste of figs on the king's sore, and he got better. Hezekiah asked, 'What will be the sign that Yahweh will heal me?' Isaiah said, 'Should the shadow on the stairway go forward ten steps or back ten steps?' Hezekiah said, 'It's easy for a shadow to go forward. Let it go back ten steps!' Isaiah cried out to Yahweh, and God made the shadow go backward ten steps on the stairway! God sees your tears too. He hears every prayer, even the ones you cry.

scenes.caption: A very sick king
scenes.art_direction: Hezekiah lying in bed, pale and weak; Isaiah standing nearby.

scenes.caption: Face to the wall
scenes.art_direction: Hezekiah turning toward the wall, praying and crying.

scenes.caption: Not even out of the courtyard
scenes.art_direction: Isaiah stopping mid-step in the courtyard as light shines on him.

scenes.caption: 'I have seen your tears'
scenes.art_direction: Golden lettering: 'I have heard your prayer. I have seen your tears.'

scenes.caption: A fig paste
scenes.art_direction: Servants mashing figs into a healing paste.

scenes.caption: The shadow goes back!
scenes.art_direction: A sundial-like stairway; the shadow moving backward ten steps; Hezekiah amazed.

memory_verse.text: I have heard your prayer. I have seen your tears.

identity_focus.core_truth: Yahweh hears my prayers and sees my tears.
identity_focus.reflection_prompt: God saw Hezekiah's tears and answered his prayer. Have you ever cried when you prayed? It's okay! God sees and cares. What would you like to tell Him?

quiz.question: What did Hezekiah do when he heard he would not recover?
options: He turned his face to the wall, prayed, and cried
quiz.explanation: He turned his face to the wall and prayed to Yahweh... and Hezekiah wept bitterly.

quiz.question: How many years did God add to Hezekiah's life?
quiz.explanation: God said, 'I will add to your days fifteen years.'

quiz.question: What sign did God give Hezekiah?
options: The shadow went back ten steps
quiz.explanation: He brought the shadow ten steps backward, by which it had gone down.

micro_prayer.text: Yahweh, thank You that You hear my prayers and see my tears. When I'm sad or scared, I can cry out to You, and You care. Amen.

companion.message: God turned a shadow backward just to show Hezekiah He was listening! He cares about every tear you cry too.

review.notes: Hezekiah's illness and expected death (2 Kings 20:1). Hezekiah's later pride with the Babylonian envoys (20:12-19) is omitted. Confirm.
